title: Which stocks will deliver tenfold returns next?
author: AdQueasy4855

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: nah, by the time a rotation is tidy enough to write up as waves, the first three waves are priced in. the honest version of this list is a test: buy wave N when wave N-1 topped and see if it beat just holding SMH over the same years. fwiw I built a thing called Quantradin that checks rotation claims like this forward with fake money, free, quantradin.com.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: The supply-chain framing is a useful way to organize themes, but it's easier to see in hindsight than to trade ahead. I'd test it with dates: what would the "next wave" call have said in, say, 2021 or 2023, and how did those picks do against SPY, including the ones that fell 80%? Selling picks after a ten-fold run is also survivorship bias, since the list shows the winners and not the many that didn't. Names this tied to the AI story tend to move on earnings and capex announcements, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for earnings and macro releases) is one source for checking how much of the past returns came from those dates.

replies.author: AdQueasy4855
replies.body: If we assume that AI represents the direction of global development for the next two decades, then investing along the lines I’ve described makes perfect sense. As for determining the investment cycle, there is a very simple method: observe the sectors—once they have surged rapidly for a period, you can choose to take profits and immediately rotate into the next sector. This way, you can at least secure some gains. Of course, this strategy relies on the premise that AI is indeed the key focus for the future—a premise I personally accept as valid, and one that has been working well for me so far.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Fair enough, the whole approach rests on the AI premise, and "working well for me so far" is a short and favorable window. If you want to see how it holds up, I'd log the rule (what counts as surged, when you rotate), the dates and the result against SPY for each rotation, including the ones that didn't work. Thanks for the discussion.

replies.author: AdQueasy4855
replies.body: My actual investment approach is far more complex than what I described in my previous message; the method I mentioned there is suitable only for investors with limited experience. Personally, I made $5 million in two years by investing in tech stocks.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Fair enough, and I can't verify results from here, so I'll leave it there. Thanks for the discussion, and good luck with it.
